To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of SLC to aqueous HPMC solution leads to an increased viscosity, which can be explained by the formation of a network structure.
the addition of SLC to aqueous solutions of the highly substituted hydrophobic cellulose derivatives HPMC leads to a shear induced transition of the intermolecular polymer interactions.

dilatant flow is observed in aqueous solutions of hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC) when the HPMC is highly substituted, when sodium lauryl sulphate (SLS) is added to the system, and at a certain concentration of SLS, i.e. in the critical micellar concentration (CMC) range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rheology of aqueous solutions containing HPMC and SLS.
the rheological behavior of aqueous HPMC solution with and without addition of SLS.
a new type of dilatant behavior in aqueous HPMC systems in the presence of SLS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dilatant behavior of aqueous HPMC/SLS solutions is due to the presence of a network of intermolecularly associated HPMC chains which can be formed in the critical micellar concentration range of SLS.
the dilatant behavior is a result of the formation of a network structure, which is caused by the interaction of the polymer segments and the surfactant molecules.
the dilatant behavior of the aqueously HPMC solutions with SLS is caused by the formation of a network, in which the HPMC segments are held together by hydrophobic interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dilatancy in the HPMC/SLS mixtures is caused by an increase in the intermolecular interaction of the polymer segments.
the addition of SLC to aqueous HPMC solution leads to an increase in viscosity and to a change in flow behavior from shear thinning to shear thickening.
the dilatant behavior of the aqueously dispersed HPMC/SLS mixtures is a result of a shear induced transition of the polymer segments from a random coiled conformation to an extended conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of anionic surfactants to aqueous solutions of hydrophobic cellulose derivatives can result in a dilatant flow, which is otherwise only found in some suspensions and in associative thickening solutions.
the rheology of HPMC/SLS solutions is highly dependent on the HPMC hydrophobicity.
dilatancy can be achieved in a system of a nonionic polymer and an anionic surfactants.
